policies.purpose: Permit additive compatibility and visual reconstruction without rewriting historical expedition truth.

allowed_migration_types.visual_reconstruction: A newer renderer may reconstruct old semantics while preserving the original pin and historical state.
allowed_migration_types.additive_registry_adapter: A new registry may understand an old ID without changing the old record.
allowed_migration_types.derived_index_rebuild: Indexes and caches may be regenerated from unchanged authoritative records.
allowed_migration_types.format_wrapper: A non-lossy wrapper may expose old data to a newer runtime while retaining the original bytes or canonical record.
allowed_migration_types.explicit_fork: A user may create a new separately identified branch; it may not masquerade as continuation of the original save.

forbidden_changes: event, visit, fault, encounter, competency or principle ledger rewrite
unvalidated capability inserted into a historical item or ship
visual reconstruction changing room or bridge semantics
rules: Existing saves remain readable through adapters before destructive conversion is considered.
Original records are retained or hash-pinned before any derived representation is produced.
A migration must state what changes, what does not change, and how rollback works.
Failure to prove non-loss results in HOLD, not automatic conversion.
A changed root set, timeline start, hidden seed, or ship blueprint commitment creates a new branch.
